provenance.notes: Procedural proxy added with the nightshades work (2026-10-17): every character from the floras in the nightshades notes (plantgen-claude project-files/nightshades/SOURCES.md), drawn by the rules its taxa hold; drawing values only where no character says them.

taxon.note: WCVP v16 accepted name Fuchsia magellanica, plant_name_id 2814960 (Library 1.0 list, read 2026-10-17).

growth_form.note: Its habit as the floras describe it, drawn by the shrub form.

growth.note: Grown to the age it is drawn at: an annual's one season, a perennial's or shrub's few years.

variants.note: One seed in the open, as the built-in species.

generator.params.note: Drawing values no character gives (fuchsias, 2026-10-17): many stems from the foot, as the dense, arching shrub in a photograph (iNaturalist 349007151) and Bailey's twiggy, cross-branched gracilis (vol. 3 p. 1301).

allometry.note: Wikipedia, 'Fuchsia magellanica' (read 2026-10-17): 1-3 m tall and wide where there is no frost; Bailey (vol. 3 p. 1301): 'Riccartonii' 6-10 ft. Its reference height is the middle of that range, 2.0 m, at its last keyframe.

traits.life_span.note: Wikipedia, 'Fuchsia magellanica' (read 2026-10-17): a sub-shrub; Bean (vol. 1 p. 576): in mild places trees 10 ft high with trunks 6 in through.

traits.height_typical_m.note: Wikipedia, 'Fuchsia magellanica' (read 2026-10-17): 1-3 m tall and wide where there is no frost; Bailey (vol. 3 p. 1301): 'Riccartonii' 6-10 ft.

traits.height_max_m.note: Bailey, Standard Cyclopedia of Horticulture vol. 3 (1914), Fuchsia magellanica 'Riccartonii', p. 1301 (read on the Internet Archive, 2026-10-17): 6-10 ft, making a trunk 3 in. diam.

traits.leaf_habit.note: Wikipedia, 'Fuchsia magellanica' (read 2026-10-17): deciduous where frosts are light; Bean (vol. 1 p. 577): the genus's leaves deciduous.

traits.leaf_arrangement.note: Bailey, Standard Cyclopedia of Horticulture vol. 3 (1914), Fuchsia magellanica, p. 1301 (read on the Internet Archive, 2026-10-17): leaves opposite or in 3s; Wikipedia: whorls of 3-4 a node, sometimes opposite; Bean (p. 577): mostly in threes at each joint.

traits.shoot_leaves.note: Leaves on a vigorous year's shoot, which no source counts: Bean (vol. 1 p. 576) has shoots grow 3 to 5 ft in a season, and a photograph (iNaturalist 126164319) shows whorls of 3 leaves about 4-6 cm apart up such a stem, so some 15 to 25 whorls

traits.leaves_per_whorl.note: Bean, Trees and Shrubs Hardy in the British Isles vol. 1 (1914), Fuchsia macrostemma, p. 577 (read on the Internet Archive, 2026-10-17): leaves mostly in threes at each joint; Bailey: opposite or in 3s.

traits.leaf_shape.note: Bailey, Standard Cyclopedia of Horticulture vol. 3 (1914), Fuchsia magellanica, p. 1301 (read on the Internet Archive, 2026-10-17): leaves lance-ovate; Wikipedia: ovate to lanceolate.

traits.leaf_apex.note: iNaturalist observation 201803461 (CC-licensed photograph, viewed 2026-10-17): the leaves taper to a fine point; Bailey (vol. 3 p. 1301) globosa: acute. No text read gives it.

traits.leaf_margin.note: Wikipedia, 'Fuchsia magellanica' (read 2026-10-17): serrate margins; Bailey (vol. 3 p. 1301): dentate.

traits.leaf_length_m.note: Wikipedia, 'Fuchsia magellanica' (read 2026-10-17): 2.5-6 cm; Bean (vol. 1 p. 577) globosa: 1-2 in.

traits.petiole_length_m.note: Wikipedia, 'Fuchsia magellanica' (read 2026-10-17): petiole 0.5-1 cm. Bailey's 'very short-petioled' (vol. 3 p. 1301) is shorter.

traits.leaf_colour.note: Bean, Trees and Shrubs Hardy in the British Isles vol. 1 (1914), Fuchsia magellanica, p. 577 (read on the Internet Archive, 2026-10-17): leaves dark green, in some forms red-purple along the stalk and veins. The colour is our reading of the words.

traits.leaf_hairs.note: Bailey, Standard Cyclopedia of Horticulture vol. 3 (1914), Fuchsia magellanica var. globosa, p. 1301 (read on the Internet Archive, 2026-10-17): leaves glabrous.

traits.twig_colour.note: Bean, Trees and Shrubs Hardy in the British Isles vol. 1 (1914), Fuchsia magellanica, p. 577 (read on the Internet Archive, 2026-10-17): red young wood (pumila), short-jointed red shoots (conica); Bailey (p. 1301): deep purple branches (discolor). The colour is our reading of the words.

traits.bark_colour.note: iNaturalist observation 159408070 (CC-licensed photograph, viewed 2026-10-17): older stems pale grey-brown; no text read describes the bark. No text read gives it.

traits.bark_texture.note: iNaturalist observation 159408070 (CC-licensed photograph, viewed 2026-10-17): the older stems' thin bark flakes; no text read describes it. No text read gives it.

traits.bark_inner_colour.note: iNaturalist observation 159408070 (CC-licensed photograph, viewed 2026-10-17): paler tan where the bark has flaked; no text read describes it. No text read gives it.

traits.pedicel_length_m.note: Wikipedia, 'Fuchsia magellanica' (read 2026-10-17): peduncle 3-4.5 cm; Bean (vol. 1 p. 577) gracilis: very slender, 1.5-2 in.

traits.flower_size_m.note: Across its sepals, which no source measures: two spreading sepals of 20-25 mm (Wikipedia 'Fuchsia magellanica') a little more than their length apart; Bean (vol. 1 p. 577) globosa's calyx 1 in.

traits.hypanthium_length_m.note: Wikipedia, 'Fuchsia magellanica' (read 2026-10-17): hypanthium magenta, 10-13 mm; Bailey (vol. 3 p. 1301): little longer than the ovary, short-cylindrical.

traits.sepal_length_m.note: Wikipedia, 'Fuchsia magellanica' (read 2026-10-17): 4 sepals, 20-25 mm; Bean (vol. 1 p. 577) globosa: 3/4 in.

traits.sepal_posture.note: Bailey, Standard Cyclopedia of Horticulture vol. 3 (1914), Fuchsia magellanica, p. 1301 (read on the Internet Archive, 2026-10-17): sepals spread wide (discolor), spreading (gracilis); photograph iNaturalist 133411246: flaring out and down.

traits.calyx_colour.note: Bean, Trees and Shrubs Hardy in the British Isles vol. 1 (1914), Fuchsia magellanica, p. 577 (read on the Internet Archive, 2026-10-17): sepals rich scarlet; Bailey (vol. 3 p. 1301): red; Wikipedia: magenta. The colour is our reading of the words.

traits.petal_length_m.note: Wikipedia, 'Fuchsia magellanica' (read 2026-10-17): 4 petals, dark purple, 10-13 mm, convolute.

traits.corolla_lobe_posture.note: Bailey, Standard Cyclopedia of Horticulture vol. 3 (1914), Fuchsia magellanica var. globosa, p. 1301 (read on the Internet Archive, 2026-10-17): petals erect; conica: erect; Wikipedia: convolute after anthesis, the skirt.

traits.flower_colour.note: Wikipedia, 'Fuchsia magellanica' (read 2026-10-17): petals dark purple; Bean (vol. 1 p. 577): rich purple; Bailey: 'blue'. The colour is our reading of the words.

traits.stamen_length_m.note: Wikipedia, 'Fuchsia magellanica' (read 2026-10-17): filaments 25-30 mm; Bailey (vol. 3 p. 1301): long-exserted.

traits.stamen_colour.note: Bean, Trees and Shrubs Hardy in the British Isles vol. 1 (1914), Fuchsia corallina, p. 577 (read on the Internet Archive, 2026-10-17): the stamens red, standing 3/4 in beyond the petals; photograph iNaturalist 133411246: red filaments.

traits.style_length_m.note: Longer than the stamens, which no source measures: Bean (vol. 1 p. 577) 'much protruded stamens, and still more protruded style'; the stamens' 25-30 mm (Wikipedia) and the photograph's style about a third longer (iNaturalist 133411246)

traits.flowering_months.note: Bean, Trees and Shrubs Hardy in the British Isles vol. 1 (1914), Fuchsia, p. 576 (read on the Internet Archive, 2026-10-17): in Britain from July until frost; Bailey (vol. 3 p. 1301): 'Riccartonii' flowers best in autumn.

traits.fruit_size_m.note: Wikipedia, 'Fuchsia magellanica' (read 2026-10-17): berry ellipsoid, 10-15 mm long.

traits.fruit_width_m.note: Wikipedia, 'Fuchsia magellanica' (read 2026-10-17): printed 0.7-0.9 mm wide, surely 7-9 mm, as the photographs show a berry about two thirds as wide as long.

traits.fruit_colour_ripe.note: iNaturalist observation 43195696 (CC-licensed photograph, viewed 2026-10-17): glossy, deep red berries; no text read gives the colour. No text read gives it.

traits.fruiting_months.note: A model estimate (confidence medium), as no source read gives it: berries ripening from August to November in Britain, after the flowers.
